programRef: ~/.claude/projects/-home-ax/memory/well-dipper-cockpit-program.md — HELM cockpit program (lane E), increment 1 of 6
statusNote: RE-SPEC #2, 2026-07-28, after Max reviewed ceb277e. His three corrections: (1) the canopy must be a faceted fighter-style ENCLOSURE — canopy above, in front, and to BOTH SIDES of the pilot — with the ribs running along the SEAMS between its flat panels. What is built is a flat WINDOW, which is why the ribs read as decoration lying on a pane: they have no seams to be. (2) The arms must be properly modelled, monitor-arm style, AFFIXED TO THE RIBS. (3) Occlusion is explicitly NOT a concern at this stage — Max wants general shape/composition right first. Handed off to a fresh session; see ~/briefings/handoff-lane-E-cockpit-enclosure-2026-07-28.md.
designDecisions: GLB metric convention: eye-point at origin, 1 unit = 1 m, Y-up, NO scale normalisation. Deliberately not the ships pipeline's mesh.scale.setScalar(1/radius) — that is a ships-manifest convention and wrong for the one object whose real-world size matters. In-game scaling happens at the 5th-pass cockpit camera.
Cockpit render resolution (match the world's pixelScale=3 third-res chunk vs. crisper) is deferred to increment 2, where both can be shown side by side for Max to judge by eye.
Screens are at the four CORNERS of the canopy (two upper, two lower), superseding the program memory's earlier 'four screens in a row above the median'. Max, this session.
No interior console/dash. The space below the median is the ship's own nose — exterior hull geometry, lit by the world rather than shadowed like the interior frame. Max, this session.
Content-to-panel assignment is NOT locked here; corners are peripheral vision, so it gets re-checked in increment 2 once the panels are legible.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The committed Blender script emits cockpit geometry as a faceted fighter-style ENCLOSURE, not a window: (a) CANOPY — flat faceted panels wrapping the pilot ABOVE, IN FRONT and to BOTH SIDES, so that turning the head in the lab's eye view finds canopy rather than empty space; (b) RIBS — running along the SEAMS where those panels meet, which is what a rib structurally IS; a rib not lying on a panel-to-panel seam is a failure; (c) SCREENS — four units, one per quadrant, each a box with a display face 50% larger than the original 0.30x0.20 m panel, a ~1 inch bezel and ~2 inch deep body, face recessed so the bezel reads, and each display-face normal within 20 degrees of its centre-to-eye vector; (d) ARMS — properly modelled monitor-style arms (segments and joints, not tapered sticks) AFFIXED TO THE RIBS; (e) NO ship nose. [Amended 2026-07-28: the earlier requirement that every arm ROOT lie outside the 70deg/16:9 frustum is RETIRED. Max resolved the ambiguity — 'arms coming from outside the player's POV' means their origin is hidden by structure, not that it sits beyond the view. Arms attach to ribs.]

verifyVia.input: Headless parse of the exported GLB: canopy panel normals and their angular coverage from the eye; each rib's proximity to a panel-to-panel seam; per screen the display-face centroid/normal, bezel width and body depth against the script's declared inch constants; each arm's attachment proximity to a rib; node inventory.
verifyVia.observable: Canopy panels present above, ahead and to both sides, together covering a stated solid angle around the eye well beyond the 70deg/16:9 frustum; every rib lies along a seam within tolerance; four display faces one per quadrant, each normal within 20 degrees of its centre-to-eye vector and area >= 1.5x the original panel; bezel and body depth match declared constants; every arm touches a rib within tolerance; no node named Hull_Nose anywhere.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The GLB carries the agreed metric convention: 1 unit = 1 metre, Y-up, the pilot's eye-point at exactly (0,0,0), and no scale normalisation anywhere in the exported node hierarchy. The exported bounding box matches the dimensions the script declares in metres.

verifyVia.input: Headless parse of the GLB JSON chunk + accessors: read every node's scale, the scene bounding box from accessor min/max, and compare against the script's declared metre constants.
verifyVia.observable: Every node scale is (1,1,1) within 1e-6; the eye-point is at the origin within 1e-4 m; the scene bounding box equals the script's declared metre dimensions within 1e-3 m; the asset is Y-up (export_yup).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The geometry is reproducible from the committed script — re-running it headless from a clean checkout produces the same mesh, so proportions can be re-authored by editing the script rather than by hand-modelling. Byte-identity of the GLB file is NOT asserted (the glTF exporter may vary metadata); geometric identity is.

verifyVia.input: Run the committed Blender script headless twice into separate output paths; decode the vertex-position and index buffers from each GLB and hash them.
verifyVia.observable: SHA-256 of the decoded position buffer and of the index buffer are identical across the two runs, for every mesh in the file.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Occlusion is MEASURED AND REPORTED, and at this stage carries NO pass/fail band. Max, reviewing ceb277e (36.93%): 'I'm not all that worried about it. I more want to get the general shape/composition right at this stage.' The original [0.25, 0.30] band came from a design he has twice replaced and is retired. The measurement is still required — it is what stops 'classic cockpit' being unfalsifiable vibes, and it is the diagnostic that revealed the old canopy rim sat entirely outside the frustum — but a band is only re-set once the enclosure form is settled.

verifyVia.input: chrome-devtools on cockpit-lab.html at :5179 — snap to the eye view, fov 70 / aspect 16:9, render the cockpit alone (Canopy_Glass hidden) against a flat background, read back framebuffer pixel counts via evaluate_script.
verifyVia.observable: A reported occluded-pixel fraction, recorded in evidence/AC-LIVE-RESULT.md alongside the analytic prediction. PASS requires Max to have accepted a band around that figure; until he does, this AC is measured-but-open, not PASS.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: cockpit-lab.html loads on the :5179 dev server and gives Max both views of the model: free orbit to spin and inspect it from outside, and an "eye" view that snaps the camera to the origin at 70 degree FOV to see it from the pilot's seat, with a placeholder background visible through the canopy opening so it reads as an opening. The CABIN LIGHT is OFF by default (Max, this session) and toggleable on. No console errors.

verifyVia.input: chrome-devtools: load http://localhost:5179/well-dipper/cockpit-lab.html (vite.config.js sets base: '/well-dipper/', so the root path 404s), await window._cockpitLab.ready, drag to orbit, switch to eye mode, list console messages.
verifyVia.observable: GLB loads and renders; orbit changes the camera pose; the eye button puts the camera at the origin with camera.fov === 70; background is visible through the aperture; zero console errors and zero failed network requests.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The lab-first gate: this increment cannot break the game. No existing file under src/ is modified (new files are permitted; none are expected), every existing *-lab.html still loads, and the vitest suite stays at its 1616-passing baseline.

verifyVia.input: git diff --stat master...feature/cockpit filtered to src/; npx vitest run from the worktree directory.
verifyVia.observable: Zero modified pre-existing files under src/; 1616 tests passing (the 15 vendor/motion-test-kit collection errors are known pre-existing noise and are excluded).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max spins the model in the lab and drops into the pilot's seat, and judges whether it reads as the angular cockpit he asked for — whether the framing at 70 degrees is something he'd want the default screensaver to play inside for long stretches, and whether the four corner screens sit where he'd actually look.

verifyVia.input: Max opens cockpit-lab.html at :5179, orbits the model, and switches to the eye view.
verifyVia.observable: Max's holistic judgement — does this read as a cockpit he wants to be inside, and does it earn the "woah, this is a real game" reaction he scoped it for? Deferred to Max; no agent renders this.

amendments.change: Corrected the verification URL from http://localhost:5179/cockpit-lab.html to http://localhost:5179/well-dipper/cockpit-lab.html, and added 'await window._cockpitLab.ready' to the input.
amendments.why: vite.config.js:7 sets base: '/well-dipper/', so the root-path URL 404s — the original input would have produced a spurious FAIL against working code. The added await is because evaluate_script otherwise races GLTFLoader. Factual correction to the verification method; the AC's substance is unchanged, so it was not re-greenlit.

amendments.change: Re-spec after Max's UAT on 1056f30. AC-FORM rewritten to boxy screens (1in bezel / 2in backing) 50% larger, carried on arms rooted outside the view frustum, two vertical canopy ribs plus a Canopy_Glass shell, and NO ship nose. AC-FRAME converted from a fixed [0.25,0.30] band to measure-and-report with the band re-set from the new form. AC-LAB now requires the cabin light off by default.
amendments.why: Max replaced the form language at UAT: screens 50% bigger and boxy on arms from outside his POV, canopy frame reduced to two vertical strips showing its protruding shape, nose removed, cabin light off. The old AC-FRAME band was working-Claude's operationalisation of 'classic cockpit' and was derived from the frame+nose design now deleted — keeping it would have forced geometry to be padded to hit a stale number. The AC's PURPOSE (stop 'classic cockpit' being unfalsifiable vibes) is preserved as a required measurement.

amendments.change: AC-FORM rewritten from a flat-window form to a faceted fighter-style ENCLOSURE (canopy above/ahead/both sides) with ribs required to lie on panel-to-panel SEAMS and arms required to be properly modelled and AFFIXED TO THE RIBS. The 'arm roots outside the frustum' clause is retired. AC-FRAME's band is held open explicitly rather than left implicitly pending.
amendments.why: Max's review of ceb277e. (1) He identified that ribs are structurally SEAMS between flat canopy panels — the build had ribs lying on a near-flat pane with no seams to follow, which is why they read as decoration. He wants a fighter-pilot enclosure: canopy above, in front and to either side. (2) He asked for real monitor-arm modelling affixed to the ribs, which RESOLVES the ambiguity working-Claude had flagged: 'outside the player's POV' means the origin is hidden by structure, not beyond the frustum. (3) He explicitly deprioritised occlusion at this stage in favour of shape and composition.
